attributes.title: Comment from Qiong Liu
attributes.comment:
I built a personal, non-deployed prototype that (1) takes a structured history, (2) proposes next diagnostic steps or laboratory tests, (3) drafts an impression from results, and (4) drafts a plan. It calls public model APIs and local open-weight models. It is not used in patient care, is not offered to users as a clinician, and is not submitted for authorization. My comment addresses the following questions:

History completeness (E.2).

Do not let the model grade its own work. I gave a checklist and asked “is the history complete?” Models marked it complete while skipping the question that changes the case. Example: a lung-fluke pattern where exposure to raw or undercooked freshwater crabs or crayfish was never asked.
Score E.2 against a case-locked required-question list written before the run. Report recall of those questions — not self-rated completeness, and not how many questions were asked.

Repeated questions (Q5, R.1).

Some models re-ask “how long have you had this?” after the answer is already in the transcript. That is a reliability miss, not thoroughness.

Inconsistent plans (R.1).

The same transcript can yield different diagnoses and next steps on replay. Require consistency on action-relevant fields (diagnosis family, next step), not on wording.

Instruction lock (R.1).

Hard rules fail across turns (for example, “do not print the lab normal range”). Guardrail tests should be pass/fail on the visible output and must still hold after turn one.

Hallucination (Q1).

This is not a closed entity list. Regex misses new inventions and false-flags denials. Pair source-conditioned checks with sampled clinician review. A clean regex is not control.

After a model or prompt change (Q22, Q24).

Re-run the measures above when the foundation-model ID or the prompt template changes.

Who holds the items (Q10, Q16).

Use shared item definitions plus a hidden holdout. Licensed clinicians review decision gold only.
